subject: Newport renewal — benchmarking & capacity uplift request
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Elliot Nash <elliot.nash@newportcommerce.com>, Procurement <procurement@newportcommerce.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Newport renewal — benchmark request before signing

Hi Elliot / team,

Thanks again for the candid conversation last week. We understand Newport is evaluating alternatives and that a short, focused benchmark is the gate for renewal approval on your side. To avoid any surprise during procurement, we'd like to propose a concrete, time-boxed benchmark and an accompanying uplift offer so you can compare apples-to-apples.

Proposed benchmark (high level):
- 48-hour throughput + P50/P95 latency run using your production prompt set (anonymized)
- Two target profiles: current baseline (your traffic) and 2x capacity stress run
- Deliverables: latency/throughput graphs, per-token cost estimate, QoS snapshot, and a short post-run findings deck

Commercial concession: if Newport signs a 12-month renewal with a committed baseline uplift (TBD), we'll provide 30 days of complimentary surge capacity for the production cutover and a one-time credit to offset migration/testing costs.

Can you confirm: (a) you can provide a sanitized prompt sample and a representative traffic trace, and (b) whether security needs a SOC2/pen-test artifact prior to kickoff? If those are green, Ben and Marissa will run the technical plan and Monica will align CS.

Tentatively available to start the week of 11/22 — happy to adapt to your timeline.

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_bench_plan_v1.pdf]
From: Elliot Nash <elliot.nash@newportcommerce.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@newportcommerce.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Nov 2027 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Newport renewal — benchmark request before signing

Karthik — appreciate the quick follow. Sorry for the delay; procurement pulled in a couple of execs.

Quick context from our side: we have a competing proof from Laura Chen at RivalModels that shows about ~12% lower per-token cost in their test, but their P95 latency spikes and they had to throttle batching to get stability. Procurement is pushing for a direct bakeoff.

We can provide:
- A 24-hour sampled traffic trace (sanitized) and a set of 50 representative prompts
- A procurement window with decision by 12/06 if results align with budget targets

Security: yes — send SOC2 and our security team (cc'ing Priya separately) will review.

What we need from you to make the comparison fair:
1) Exact test configuration (batching, model variant, quantization, seq_len)
2) Expected per-token cost at 1x and 2x throughput
3) Commitment to a fixed test environment (no capacity swapping mid-run)

If you can get back with a short scope and a kickoff date this week, that would be ideal.

—Elliot
VP, Product
Newport Commerce
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Nov 2027 14:20:00 -0800
Subject: INTERNAL: Newport bakeoff plan (draft)

Team — quick triage following Elliot's note. Draft plan below; need signoff on discount and credit numbers from Karthik.

Technical run plan:
- Duration: 48 hours (we recommend 48 vs 24 to capture diurnal variance)
- Workload: use Newport's 24h sampled trace + 50 prompts; run baseline then 2x stress phase for 6 hours
- Model/config: rwin-2.7b (quantized FP8), batch window 60ms, dynamic KV cache enabled, max seq 1024
- Metrics: P50/P95 latency, 99th customer-visible tail, tokens/sec, error rate, memory OOMs, token cost per 1M tokens
- Test isolation: pinned dedicated GPUs for the run; no routing changes for test duration

Commercial proposal (draft):
- 30% off incremental surge usage for first 30 days (applies to uplift above current committed baseline)
- One-time $25k testing/migration credit applied at contract signature
- If benchmark meets agreed QoS targets, 12-month renewal with a 10% uplift commitment on baseline capacity

Attachments: mutual action plan template and bench plan (I attached both).

Questions for Karthik:
- Approve the 30% surge discount + $25k credit?
- Approve offer to lock a 10% uplift commitment for the 12-month renewal?

I'll prepare the benchmark harness and a short runbook for Newport engineers.

Ben
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: mutual_action_plan_nov22.xlsx]
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Elliot Nash <elliot.nash@newportcommerce.com>, Procurement <procurement@newportcommerce.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 17 Nov 2027 09:00:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Newport renewal — benchmark request before signing

Elliot — thanks for the context and for flagging the RivalModels result. We agree a fair bakeoff is the right path. Below is a short, binding scope for the benchmark so procurement can compare consistently: 

Scope (final):
- Run window: 48 hours starting week of 11/22 (we can shift to your schedule)
- Environment: dedicated GPU pool pinned for the run (no scaling changes)
- Config: rwin-2.7b (quantized) with 60ms batching window, max_seq 1024
- Deliverables: bench report (P50/P95), QoS snapshot, per-token cost at 1x & 2x, run artifacts (logs), and a short exec deck

Commercial (final):
- 30% discount on incremental surge usage for first 30 days post-signature
- $25,000 one-time credit for migration/testing costs applied at signature
- If bench meets the QoS targets (P95 tail < 250ms, error rate < 0.2%), we commit to a 12-month renewal with a 10% uplift baseline at the nominated price

Next steps:
1) Newport provides sanitized prompt set and sampled trace by EOD 11/19
2) We schedule a 30-minute kickoff (bench tech alignment) the day before the run
3) Our security pack (SOC2 summary + pen-test attest) will be shared in this thread before kickoff

Attaching the bench plan and mutual action plan. If procurement signs off on the scope, we'll publish a DocuSign MAA and lock the kickoff slot.

Karthik
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_bench_plan_v1.pdf]
[Attachment: mutual_action_plan_nov22.xlsx]
From: Elliot Nash <elliot.nash@newportcommerce.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@newportcommerce.com>, Priya Malhotra <priya.malhotra@newportcommerce.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2027 16:36:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Newport renewal — benchmark request before signing

Karthik / team — this looks good. Newport will provide the sanitized prompt set and the sampled trace by COB 11/19. Priya (cc) from security will need the SOC2 summary and the redwood QoS snapshot before the run; please include any attestations you have.

Procurement: please confirm the decision window is still 12/06. If the benchmark shows parity on QoS and cost, we can move to a clean renewal. We will also perform a short production pilot during the 30-day surge period (production read-only traffic) to validate end-to-end behavior.

One ask: include a short section in the mutual action plan clarifying rollback and data-retention behavior during the surge/pilot. I'll push that to procurement.

Thanks — ready to kick off next week.

—Elliot
VP, Product
Newport Commerce
[Attachment: Newport_procurement_note.pdf]
